questions.stem: A 35-year-old man has needed a routine annual medical examination for his employment. His ECG result showed prolongation of the PR interval to more than 0.22 s. In which one of the following sites in the heart is the abnormal conducting system situated?
questions.explanation: First-degree AV block indicates abnormality at the AV node, situated in the right atrium.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with shortness of breath and is diagnosed with mitral stenosis. On auscultation, she has an opening snap with mid-diastolic murmur with presystolic accentuation. At which one of the following anatomical sites will these auscultatory findings be best heard?
options: Sternal end of the 2nd left intercostal space
5th left intercostal space in the midclavicular line
Sternal end of 2nd right intercostal space
Left lower sternal border at the 5th intercostal space
Opposite the 4th left costal cartilage behind the sternum
questions.explanation: The mitral valve is best heard over the apex beat, at the 5th left intercostal space in the midclavicular line.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 50-year-old man complains of symptoms of heartburn and gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD). He is due to have an oesophagogastroduodenoscopy. At what level from the incisors will the normal gastro-oesophageal junction be found?
questions.explanation: The normal gastro-oesophageal junction is 40 cm from the incisors.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 45-year-old man is due to undergo a laparoscopic Nissen fundoplication as an anti-reflux operation for his gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD). Which one of the following structures is in danger of being damaged?
questions.explanation: The right and left vagus nerves form plexuses around the oesophagus and are vulnerable during anti-reflux surgery.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A girl is born with severe respiratory distress as a result of a congenital diaphragmatic hernia. This was diagnosed antenatally. Through which one of the following foramina in the diaphragm has the hernia occurred?
questions.explanation: Congenital diaphragmatic hernia most commonly occurs through the posterolateral Bochdalek foramen.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man, a smoker, presents with a 3-day history of worsening headaches and shortness of breath with swelling of his face, upper chest and neck. Which one of the following structures is compressed causing his symptoms?
questions.explanation: These symptoms are typical of superior vena cava syndrome from compression by mediastinal tumour.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 62-year-old man complaining of dysphagia has been diagnosed with carcinoma of the middle third of the oesophagus. Which group of lymph nodes will this cancer spread to in the first instance?
questions.explanation: Lymph nodes behind the pericardium on the oesophagus drain the middle and lower thoracic oesophagus first.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 60-year-old man presents with a large carcinoma of the upper left lung. A chest X-ray confirms the diagnosis and also shows marked elevation of the left hemidiaphragm. Which one of the following nerves is affected by the carcinoma causing elevation of the left dome?
questions.explanation: The phrenic nerve supplies the diaphragm; infiltration causes paralysis and elevation of the hemidiaphragm.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition
